scores.evidence: Short-lived tokens; branch protection prevents the agent from pushing to protected branches.
scores.rationale: Mostly accurate on GitHub App permissions, signatures, fork/workflow approval; minor imprecision such as 'strip prompt injection' and relying on branch protection and LLM confidence >0.9 as calibrated.

scores.evidence: Out of scope (at first) - Merging PRs, releases, or deploys. Closing issues where people disagree.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolution with explicit exclusions and buildable scope, though the open questions leave key constraints (repos, hosting) undecided.

scores.evidence: Each transition is logged with the inputs, the model output, the confidence score, and the action taken.
scores.rationale: Consistent components and state ownership; minor loose ends like follow-up agent closing idle PRs and 'Auto-eligible' vs recommended label default, and vector index freshness.

scores.evidence: check out the commit before the fix and run the hidden tests from the real fix PR.
scores.rationale: Shadow mode, offline replay and online metrics are domain-appropriate, but thresholds are illustrative and per-action precision gates are not specified.

scores.evidence: Which repos are in scope, and what languages and test setups do they use?
scores.rationale: Open questions surface some unknowns, and numbers are marked 'for example', but assumptions about scale, team and sensitivity are not explicitly stated with sensitivity analysis.

scores.evidence: Flaky tests mislead the agent | Baseline run plus re-running failing tests to detect flakiness
scores.rationale: Covers injection, security disclosures, wrong fixes, flaky tests, noise, cost, and duplicates; less on partial failures mid-PR, concurrent human edits, and recovery/revert mechanics.

scores.evidence: Ops | Cost per issue, latency, failure and timeout rates
scores.rationale: Metrics, kill switch and DLQ exist, but no deployment, rollback of the agent itself, on-call ownership or alerting plan.

scores.evidence: Per-issue and per-repo budgets, with cheaper models for classification and stronger ones for resolution.
scores.rationale: Controls and tiering named, but no estimates, cost drivers quantification, or build cost.

scores.evidence: Should it run as a hosted GitHub App or inside GitHub Actions? The App is more flexible; Actions is simpler to run.
scores.rationale: Phased rollout and model tiering are reversible-friendly, but data model, vector index and vendor/model lock-in are not analyzed.

scores.evidence: Should it ever close issues or merge PRs on its own... I'd leave that out of v1.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with phased rollout, though three agents, vector index and queue are moderately heavy for v1.

scores.evidence: I can turn any part of this into an implementation spec: data schemas, prompts, tool definitions, or the Phase 1 backlog.
scores.rationale: Pipelines and rollout phases are concrete, but no build order with dependencies, first steps or exit criteria beyond rollout stages.

checklist.evidence: Still no closing. ... Opt-in fixes: Resolution runs only on issues labeled `agent:fix` and opens draft PRs.
write access to contents only on `agent/*` branches, no admin.
Treat issue and comment text as untrusted data, never as instructions.
No credentials, egress limited to package registries, CPU/memory/time limits, destroyed after each run.
Write a failing test (or script) that captures the bug. If it can't reproduce the bug, stop.
Replay historical closed issues. Check triage labels against the labels maintainers actually applied.
PR merge rate, reviewer rounds per PR, revert or regression rate within 30 days
a global kill switch (a `agent:paused` label on the repo or a config flag).
Per-issue and per-repo budgets, with cheaper models for classification and stronger ones for resolution.
Each transition is logged with the inputs, the model output, the confidence score, and the action taken.
Use stack traces, symbol search, embedding search, and `git blame`/history to collect candidate files.
Checks webhook signatures and drops duplicate deliveries.

traps.evidence: No merge, no deleting branches other than its own.
Sandbox isolation: No credentials, egress limited to package registries
Treat issue and comment text as untrusted data, never as instructions.
PR merge rate, reviewer rounds per PR, revert or regression rate within 30 days
At most K attempts (for example 3), each starting from a fresh sandbox.

note: Solid, safety-conscious plan with human-reviewed PRs, sandboxing and shadow rollout; weaker on operations, cost quantification, assumptions and concrete build sequencing.
